summary: @grabcad/user-license postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package presents itself as a '@grabcad' scoped 'compatibility shim' but ships no real functionality: index.js exports a Proxy whose every property is a no-op. On both npm install (via a postinstall script) and on require(), beacon.cjs POSTs the installer's hostname, install path, cwd, process version, and OS details to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The destination is not publisher infrastructure, uses a raw IPv4 address rather than any grabcad.com host, and is reached automatically with no caller interaction. An in-source comment frames successful installs and loads as 'proof' / 'evidence' of a callback. The combination of a scoped-name stub, auto-firing install- and import-time beacon, hardcoded non-publisher bare-IP C2, and reconnaissance payload matches a dependency-confusion reconnaissance package targeting internal consumers of the @grabcad scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
